statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 22 of 100 in the watch band, three points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 84 and confidence is high at 80.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns WATCH for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, the two unobserved checkpoints closest to the verified consumer price print. The conditional path peaks at 22 in the current slot, eases to 21 across the Michigan release and then steps under the watch band from 15:00 UTC, so no slot in the forward window reaches the block threshold.
headline: The August consumer price report is verified at 0.4% monthly, 3.4% annual and core 0.3%, and NQ carries a 1.04% gain at 29,437 into the 13:30 UTC cash open, about sixty points under its 29,499.50 session high, with VIX down to 16.02 and the ten-year back at 4.926% after touching 5.005%, leaving tail at 22 in the watch band and stress extreme at 84.
body:
The August consumer price report released at 12:30 UTC is now verified against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release itself. All items rose 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis and 3.4% over the twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month and 2.4% over the year. The monthly core figure is one tenth above the published consensus and the annual core figure is in line. That is the first assessment in this sequence that carries a confirmed outcome rather than an open release.

The observed price path is a firm but not one-way response. Two independent feeds agree that NQ traded 29,437 to 29,438 at 13:16 UTC, up 1.04% against a 29,135.25 previous close, after posting a session high of 29,499.50 to 29,500.25. Price therefore sits roughly sixty points, or about 0.2%, below that high, so a retracement has been granted rather than refused. The prior hour recorded price within three points of a 29,339.75 high; the release lifted the market a further 160 points and the extension has since eased. The session low, reported between 29,040.50 and 29,120.75 depending on how each feed defines the session, was set before the release.

Cross-asset evidence is aligned risk-positive on the surface and conflicted underneath. VIX is 16.02, down roughly 10% on the day, with a 15.85 to 17.71 range that shows event premium bleeding out rather than building. The ten-year spiked to 5.005% on the print and has retraced to 4.926%, below the previous close. The two-year, however, is 4.596% and near its 4.611% day high, so the front end is holding a hawkish repricing while the long end unwinds it. WTI is $99.22 and Brent $104.50, down about 3.2% and 2.9%, easing a four-day oil-led drawdown in which the indexes closed lower each session. Futures markets price roughly a 70% chance of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September decision.

Tail is scored at 22. The amplifiers that argue for more are the post-release upward extension, an aligned volatility and oil backdrop, and a cash open falling inside this clock-hour after four consecutive lower closes, a configuration that has produced mean-reversion failure before. The evidence that holds it in the watch band is that the repricing looks orderly: a retracement from the high has already occurred, implied volatility is decaying, the yield reaction has been unwound at the long end, and the front-end and long-end conflict argues for two-way rather than persistent one-way structure. Event importance and a 70% hike probability into next week raise stress, which stays extreme at 84, rather than tail.

Confidence is 80. The release outcome is confirmed from the primary source, current levels are corroborated by two independent price feeds, and yields, volatility, oil and the forward calendar were all retrieved directly. The shared Finviz context collected at 11:51 UTC is roughly 94 minutes old and reports partial collection status, so it was treated as stale supplementary background only and carries no weight in the current price-path reading. What is not observed is the opening auction itself, which begins seconds after this assessment cutoff and is framed conditionally throughout the forward window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 13:00 UTC on 10 September to 12:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 24 with the mode trend-down in the slot spanning the previous day's cash open, the highest reading of the whole window and still one point below the block threshold. Tail then fell to 17 and 14 as price discovery stayed orderly and held a 14 to 19 band through that afternoon with the mode mixed, recording event/whipsaw at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC normalised into an 11 to 15 band, the quietest stretch of the window. From 06:00 UTC the mode turned trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14, 15 and 14 as the overnight advance extended, stalled and was bought back. The final slot lifts to 21 with the mode event/whipsaw, the hour in which the consumer price report was released but its outcome was not yet verifiable. Stress never left the extreme band, running 81 to 88, while confidence held 84 to 89 until that last slot, where it fell to 70 on the unverified release.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the remainder of the 11 September session and then spends its last sixteen slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 22 in the current slot, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open, and eases to 21 across the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and both sit below the 25 block threshold. The path then steps down through 18, 16 and 15 into the midday lull on the assumption that post-release volatility keeps decaying and retracements keep being granted, holds 15 across the 18:00 UTC budget statement, and lifts to 16 and then 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly rebalancing concentrates. From the 21:00 UTC futures halt the score collapses to 8 and then to a 5 to 6 floor, which represents gap risk carried into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen rather than any intraday mechanism, since the mean-reversion failure mode being scored cannot occur while the market is closed. Stress decays from extreme through high and into the moderate band across the closure, and confidence drifts from 80 to 65 on assessment age alone.

forecast.analysis: August CPI printed at 12:30 UTC: 0.4% monthly, 3.4% annual, core 0.3% and 2.4%. NQ traded 29,437 at 13:16 UTC, up 1.04% and about sixty points under its 29,499.50 session high. VIX eased to 16.02 and the ten-year retraced a 5.005% spike to 4.926%. The 13:30 UTC cash open is the first unobserved checkpoint.
